theme_overview: A selector ranks candidates by a measured score whose differences are smaller than the replication spread of the measurement, and compares challengers against a dead baseline. Looking for implementations of indifference zones in selection and of racing procedures that stop when a difference is not resolvable.
goal: implementation anchors for indifference-zone selection and racing under measurement noise
why_problem: rank order is decided by differences smaller than the measurement noise
assumptions: the replication spread of the score is known
